newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's poll lead hits three-year low.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's poll lead hits three-year low.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party's lead over Britain's ruling Conservatives has plunged to its lowest level for nearly three years, according to an opinion poll.

The latest NOP poll for The Sunday Times newspaper shows the gap between the two parties has closed to 14 points from 23, pointing to the start of the recovery Conservative Party strategists had hoped for.
The poll gives Labour 47 percent support, down five points since October 3, while the Conservatives scored 33 percent, a four-point improvement.
Prime Minister John Major must call a general election by next May.
Major is ahead of Labour Party leader Tony Blair on sincerity, with 28 percent saying they can believe what the prime minister says against 24 percent for Blair.
NOP interviewed 1,579 people face-to-face at 78 sampling points across Britain on Thursday. -- London newsroom 0171 542 7947
